item.title: Finesse evolution in a bichromatic cavity under blue and red resonant illumination in vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2611.00277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The long-term performance of high-finesse optical cavities depends on the stability of their mirror coatings under vacuum and under continuous exposure to high circulating power. In cavities supporting multiple wavelengths, a central question is whether degradation at one wavelength compromises performance at another. Understanding this interplay is essential for those cavity quantum electrodynamics experiments that need diverse optical fields for cavity stabilization, trapping, and light--matter coupling. Here, we investigate wavelength-dependent degradation and recovery of a bichromatic cavity with high-reflectivity coating at 455 nm and 671 nm in vacuum. Cavity ring-down measurements reveal a decrease in the 455 nm finesse from 7.7*10^3 to 1.9*10^3 after 11 hours of continuous exposure to high circulating power. Simultaneous measurements show no measurable degradation at 671 nm. Continuous operation at 671 nm, instead, produces no measurable degradation at either wavelength under the tested conditions. Comparison of oxygen depletion and Avrami-type loss models indicates kinetics compatible with nucleation and growth, without uniquely identifying the microscopic mechanism. We demonstrate partial recovery of the finesse with illumination at 455 nm in air. Our results indicate a wavelength dependence of laser-induced optical damage in bichromatic cavities and provide an estimate of the blue light intensity that can be safely used in such cavities.
item.dc:creator: M. S. Caracas Nu\~nez, A. Kadakkavattathu, G. Gatta, L. Duca, N. Mizukami, C. Sias

item.title: Nuclear Charge Radii from Precision Bound-Electron g-Factor Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2611.00343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An efficient method to determine absolute nuclear charge radii from high-precision bound-electron g-factor measurements in hydrogenlike ions is put forward. Assuming that a nuclear model independent radius determination is possible, we demonstrate that this method can improve the precision of the nuclear radius for several poorly known heavy isotopes by up to two orders of magnitude compared to current literature values, by utilizing recent breakthroughs in the quantum electrodynamics (QED) theory of the bound-electron g-factor [B. Sikora, V. A. Yerokhin, C. H. Keitel, and Z. Harman, Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 123001 (2025)]. This opens a new, independent pathway for testing nuclear structure models and resolving nuclear structure anomalies.
item.dc:creator: Bastian Sikora

item.title: $^{85}$Rb electromagnetically induced transparency and absorption on two collinear $5S_{1/2}\rightarrow5P_{1/2}\rightarrow5D_{3/2}\rightarrow 25F_{5/2}$ three-photon cascade schemes
item.description: arXiv:2611.00416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a comprehensive study of three-photon electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and absorption (EIA) in room-temperature Rb vapor. Using the cascade system $5S_{1/2}\rightarrow5P_{1/2}\rightarrow5D_{3/2}\rightarrow 25F_{5/2}$ in $^{85}$Rb, we explore two collinear laser-beam configurations. The detunings of the upper two lasers of the cascade system are varied. In both configurations, the probe transmission maps contain rich sets of EIT/EIA features and substructures. To explain these, we utilize a dressed-atom and a quantum Monte Carlo trajectory method. The latter includes 108 relevant fine- and hyperfine-structure levels and their magnetic substates, accounting for coherent optical drives, optical pumping, atom recycling, electromagnetic decays via the $5P_{J}$ levels, and velocity-changing and hyperfine collisions. We find quantum-trajectory solutions of the Lindblad master equation, which show good agreement with experimental data and aid in finding physical explanations for the observed spectra. To further explore collision-induced spectral features, collisional loss of EIT/EIA visibility, velocity-changing and hyperfine collisions, we acquire spectra in Rb cells with 50 and 500~mTorr of Ar gas. Our work is of interest to studies of multi-level EIT systems that underpin emerging quantum technologies, where accurate accounting of internal atomic structure, laser beam geometry, optical pumping, transit time, and collisional effects is critical.
item.dc:creator: Shuaijie Li, Alisher Duspayev, Georg Raithel

item.title: Coherent heat-bath configuration interaction with many-body perturbation theory for multivalent atoms
item.description: arXiv:2611.00731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Combinatorial growth of configuration-interaction spaces limits accurate calculations as the valence-electron number and orbital space increase. To reduce the size of the configuration-interaction space, we develop coherent heat-bath configuration interaction in a configuration-state-function basis and combine it with many-body perturbation theory. Configurations are selected by thresholding their coherent couplings to target wave functions, and a perturbative correction recovers residual valence correlation. For Al, a stringent threshold gives about 16-37 fold compression with excitation-energy deviations from the uncompressed calculations below 0.74 /cm; a looser threshold gives 63-113 fold compression with a maximum deviation of 18.22 /cm. For Si and P, roughly threefold to eightfold compression is achieved with maximum relative deviations of approximately 0.70% and 0.32%, respectively, for optical excitation energies. The perturbative correction improves the accuracy of all calculated total energies. These results support extending the method to high-precision calculations in more complex atomic systems.
item.dc:creator: Shi-Cheng Yu, Zhen-Xiang Zhong, Cheng-Bin Li

item.title: Universal Threshold Memory in Bound-State Recapture
item.description: arXiv:2611.01056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Driven slowly, a quantum system forgets how it was driven. We show that a bound state taken slowly to its continuum threshold and back does not. The recaptured fraction depends on the ratio of the approach and return rates, however slow both are. The two rates set the sizes of two threshold packets whose phase-sensitive overlap fixes recapture. Common slowing preserves their size ratio. A factorized treatment of approach and return misses this dependence. For a short-range $s$-wave state whose inverse scattering length touches zero quadratically in time, we obtain the dependence in closed form, with the maximum $1/\varphi^2$ at matched rates, where $\varphi$ is the golden ratio. A ratio of three recaptured fractions makes this threshold memory accessible with finite pulses. For radio-frequency-dressed $^{85}$Rb halo dimers with half-pulse widths of 30 and $120~\mu$s, coupled-channel calculations give this ratio within $0.5\%$ of its slow-limit value.
item.dc:creator: Sajad Azizi

item.title: Dual-Space Analysis of Vortex Configurations and Rotational Energy in a 2D Optical Lattice
item.description: arXiv:2611.02473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the effects of a stationary two-dimensional periodic optical lattice on a rotating Bose--Einstein condensate confined by an isotropic harmonic trap. Within the mean-field description, the condensate is modeled by the two-dimensional Gross--Pitaevskii equation in the rotating frame and solved numerically using an imaginary-time split-step Crank--Nicolson method to obtain stationary vortex states. We examine how the lattice depth, lattice wave vector, particle number, and angular velocity influence the vortex configurations, real-space density, momentum-space density, and energetics of the condensate. We find that the stationary periodic lattice significantly modifies vortex nucleation and spatial organization: vortices emerge progressively with increasing angular velocity and, for sufficiently strong lattice strength, undergo rearrangement and merging. Importantly, changes in the vortex configuration are directly reflected in the momentum-space density, demonstrating that vortex nucleation and rearrangement produce pronounced modifications of the condensate momentum distribution. We further analyze the energy per particle and rotational energy as functions of the angular velocity and find that the presence of the optical lattice substantially alters the rotational response of the condensate. In particular, the rotational energy is progressively reduced at higher angular velocities as the lattice strength is increased. These results demonstrate how a stationary periodic optical lattice modifies vortex formation, momentum-space structure, and rotational energetics of a rotating trapped Bose--Einstein condensate.
item.dc:creator: Avra Banerjee

item.title: The Valence and Inner Shell Ionization Properties of Sr I - III by Non-Thermal Electrons in Kilonovae
item.description: arXiv:2611.00335v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The presence of strontium (Z = 38) was identified from spectra of the first multi-messenger kilonova transient, AT2017gfo, with the evolution of its spectral signature indicating a rapidly changing ionization balance. Interpretation of spectra at later times requires a more detailed understanding of recombination and ionization processes, including ionization by `non-thermal' electrons produced by beta decay. Published measurements of the ionization cross sections of Sr I and Sr II show complex structures likely arising from excitation autoionization. Using the Flexible Atomic Code we report calculations of the valence and inner shell ionization cross sections for Sr I, Sr II, and Sr III, and recover similar structures in the ionization cross sections. Though no measurements exist for Sr III, the calculations suggest negligible contributions from excitation autoionization. These new data are incorporated into Spencer-Fano models of non-thermal electron degradation and coupled to an ionization balance solver. The effects of excitation autoionization, treated as excitation with the additional production of an Auger electron, on the degradation spectra of non-thermal are explored. Calculations at both level- and configuration-average resolution return ion fractions that agree within 5-20%. The calculations probe the impact of including final-charge-state-resolved branching ratios for inner shell ionization which result in multi-ionization events from successive Auger cascades. Omission of these branching ratios is shown to have large impacts on the ionization balance. The calculated cross sections will be provided on Zenodo.
item.dc:creator: Steven Bromley, Luke Shingles, Evan Garbe, Niall McElroy, Connor Ballance, Michael Fogle, Phillip Stancil, Stuart Loch

item.title: Reversibility of Nonequilibrium Dynamics in a Unitary Fermi Gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.00563v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We theoretically describe and experimentally observe the reversibility of a nonequilibrium state in a unitary Fermi gas confined in a time-dependent trap. Unlike the equilibrium case, reversibility out of equilibrium imposes a stringent condition: the accumulated dynamical phase must be an integer multiple of $2\pi$, i.e., $\Delta\phi = 2\omega_{0} s(T) = 2n\pi$, where $\omega_{0}$ is the initial trapping frequency and $s(T)$ is the rescaled time after a total evolution time $T$. We demonstrate the reversibility of an initial nonequilibrium state in an isotropic unitary Fermi gas by driving the optical trap through a round trip. We find two types of reversible pathways, the space-time scaling-invariant and polynomial shortcut-to-adiabaticity (STA) protocols. The phase condition restricts the round-trip time $T$ to discrete values, a distinguishing feature of nonequilibrium dynamics. Our work establishes a clear criterion for the quantum control of nonequilibrium many-body systems beyond linear response and provides practical pathways to reversibility.
item.dc:creator: Xi-Zhi Wu, Xiangchuan Yan, Xin Xie, Dali Sun, Seong-Ho Shinn, Adolfo del Campo, Kaijun Jiang

item.title: Pump-scheme dependence of few-emitter lasers: exact multilevel correlations and photon statistics
item.description: arXiv:2611.01205v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Few-emitter laser models usually replace the excitation cycle of the gain medium by a single Markovian pump jump of a two-level emitter. We test this replacement with the cavity and laser-transition parameters held fixed and the two-level pump rate fitted to the same mean photon number, using an exact damping-basis continued-fraction solution of the cavity--emitter master equation for $N$ identical $d$-level emitters with arbitrary independent incoherent transitions and one cavity-coupled transition, in the known reduced space of level populations and lasing coherences. First, a pump-quantum filtration shows that the inter-emitter coherence of $\Lambda$ and ladder media starts at second rather than first order in the pump; we evaluate its leading coefficient from the exact finite-system series and map the recycling rate at which its sign changes. Second, at matched photon number, rate-limited steps in the pump cycle push the long-time output-counting Fano factor of two and three emitters well below one: for two emitters it reaches 0.66 at a mean cavity occupation of 0.3 and is still 0.74 at an occupation of one, where $g^{(2)}(0)$ is within 3% of unity, because the anticorrelation sits at delays of about half a cavity lifetime rather than at zero delay. For two and three emitters the fitted two-level model gets both statistics wrong and places the output above the shot-noise level. Against independent single-emitter lasers at the same output, the common cavity erodes rather than enhances this single-emitter effect.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Hartmann

item.title: Inducing cooperative dynamics in an inhomogeneous many-emitter ensemble with a pulse sequence
item.description: arXiv:2611.02973v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Driving a many-particle quantum system with an appropriately tuned external field can give rise to features in its nonequilibrium dynamics that are absent in the equilibrium counterpart. Cooperative dynamics in a dense ensemble of quantum emitters manifested through superradiance, a burst in the emission intensity as a function of time, is typically suppressed by spectral disparities among emitters in the ensemble. We demonstrate the enhancement of cooperative dynamics in a spectrally inhomogeneous ensemble of quantum emitters when it is driven by a periodic pulse sequence. Using both a semi-analytical mean-field solution and a digital quantum simulation, we examine the coherence of the pulse-driven ensemble and the intensity of the emitted radiation as a function of the spectral disparity in the ensemble, as a function of time, the number of atoms in the system, and as a function of the inter-pulse delay. We identify clear signatures of the enhanced cooperative dynamics for the pulse-driven inhomogeneous ensemble when dephasing in the dynamics of the ensemble is suppressed by a sufficient number of pulses during the individual emitter lifetime. These results demonstrate a post-fabrication tuning knob based on externally applied control fields for the dynamics of the many-emitter ensemble.
item.dc:creator: Vincent P. Iglesias-Cardinale, Shreekanth S. Yuvarajan, Herbert F. Fotso

item.title: Brillouin comb line amplifiers for optical atomic clocks
item.description: arXiv:2611.03038v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optical atomic clocks outperform the microwave clocks at the heart of current timing and navigation infrastructure by orders-of-magnitude, and recent progress in on-chip integration provides the opportunity to widely deploy them. Conventionally, a narrow linewidth laser interrogates the atomic transition, and an optical frequency comb divides its stabilised frequency (hundreds of terahertz) down to a microwave that is electronically countable. The laser(s) impose a significant size, weight, power and cost penalty, which is a current barrier to low-cost, scalable, fully on-chip optical clocks. Here, we position the frequency comb as the central engine of the clock by using Brillouin-amplified comb lines for atomic spectroscopy, which eliminates the need for stable clock lasers. Amplified comb lines reach an ultra-low frequency noise floor of $6\,\mathrm{Hz^2/Hz}$ at $30\,\mathrm{kHz}$ offset, an order-of-magnitude below a high-end commercial fibre laser. We realize a clock based on the $\mathrm{5S}_{1/2}\rightarrow\mathrm{5D}_{5/2}$ transition in $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ with competitive fractional frequency stability of $2\times10^{-13}$ at $\tau = 1\,\mathrm{s}$, averaging to $9\times10^{-15}$ at $\tau = 1000\,\mathrm{s}$. Lastly, we demonstrate a photonic chip-integrated Brillouin amplifier with a record 62.9 dB gain and up to 40 dB transferred noise suppression when pumped with a simple, low-cost diode laser. This opens a new route to compact optical clocks and enables use of atomic transitions lacking low-noise lasers by broadening a comb to the required wavelength and amplifying single lines.
item.dc:creator: Ryan L. Russell, Lachlan Pointon, Sarah Katherine Scholten, Choon Kong Lai, Lisa-Sophie Haerteis, Cong Tinh Bui, Alvaro Casas Bedoya, Andreas Boes, Duk Yong Choi, Stephen J. Madden, Andre Luiten, Benjamin J. Eggleton, Moritz Merklein

item.title: Two heavy impurities immersed in light few-boson systems with noninteger dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2209.00578v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the spectrum and structure of two heavy bosonic impurities immersed in a light boson system with noninteger dimensions $D$ by means of the Born-Oppenheimer approximation. The ratio between the energies of two consecutive many-body bound states, which follows an Efimov-type geometrical scaling law when the heavy-light pair has a resonant $s$-wave interaction, is found to be a function of the mass asymmetry, number of light bosons, and effective dimension $D$. Furthermore, the wave function is computed, and its behavior is explored for different system configurations. To exemplify our results, we consider mixtures of two heavy cesium atoms interacting with up to two lithium atoms, which are systems of current experimental interest.
item.dc:creator: R. M. Francisco, D. S. Rosa, T. Frederico

item.title: Fully relativistic calculation of thermal shifts in spectra of hydrogen molecular ion
item.description: arXiv:2610.22843v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Within a fully relativistic framework, we discuss the one-loop self-energy correction, generalized to the presence of external blackbody radiation, for a bound electron in the hydrogen molecular ion. The calculations rely on the thermal part of the photon propagator from finite-temperature quantum electrodynamics. The ADKB method, which extends the dual kinetic balance condition to axially symmetric systems, is adopted together with a B-spline-based trial function. The results are obtained within the Born-Oppenheimer adiabatic approximation. Thermal shift for the ground term of the hydrogen molecular ion is computed as a function of the internuclear distance. Including this correction, we present the resulting shifts of the vibrational levels. The analysis focuses on the dynamical effect, a comparison is made with data available in the current literature.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Reiter, A. A. Anikin, A. A. Kotov, D. A. Glazov, T. A. Zalialiutdinov, D. A. Solovyev

item.title: Characteristics of VHF and UHF band detection using Stark shifting in Rydberg-atom sensors
item.description: arXiv:2610.40952v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a characterization of the sensitivity of broadband electric field measurements in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands using AC stark shifting of Rydberg states. The dependence of the sensitivity and dynamic range of the field measurements using nD5/2 states of cesium for principal quantum numbers n= 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 is presented, detailing the intricacies involved. The frequencies considered for the measurement range from 50 MHz to 900 MHz for which a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell is used to excite the Rydberg atoms with the RF fields. The relative sensitivities achieved for various principal quantum numbers are presented. A general trend of better sensitivity for higher principal quantum numbers is observed. This work paves the way for a better understanding of the AC Stark dependent field measurements using Rydberg sensors.
item.dc:creator: Rajavardhan Talashila, Noah Schlossberger, David S. La Mantia, Abby Halasi-Kun, Baran Kayim, Michael A. Viray, Robert Wyllie, Christopher L. Holloway, Nikunjkumar Prajapati

item.title: Quantum linear solvers for quantum chemistry: prospects of exponential quantum advantage
item.description: arXiv:2607.08220v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum linear solvers (QLSs) offer the potential for quantum advantage in solving quantum chemical problems, but assessing such an advantage hinges on determining condition number ($\kappa$) scaling, which itself is computationally challenging. While a recent work applied the HHL algorithm to single-reference linearized coupled cluster (SRLCC), the validity of the framework is restricted to weakly correlated regimes. We thus begin by extending QLS-SRLCC to its multi-reference form, the internally contracted multi-reference LCC (QLS-icMRLCC). We then analyze $\kappa$ scaling across a diverse range of systems as well as bases in both QLS-SRLCC and QLS-icMRLCC, using three complementary diagnostics that range from explicit computations to use of indirect structural indicators: (i) direct calculations of $\kappa$, (ii) scaling of the ratio of maximum to minimum diagonal entries of an $A$ matrix, and (iii) structural analyses of the $A$ matrices based on a recently proposed conjecture that we adapt to the QLS-LCC problem. The three approaches yield broadly consistent predictions, with our numerical results indicating a slow-growing $\kappa$ scaling in system size for the sampled systems. For icMRLCC, however, the observed behaviour depends on the reference active space, leaving the broader prospects of quantum advantage with it less certain. This finding, when combined with our arguments on sub-linear scaling of sparsity (when excitation rank>2), supports the prospects of exponential advantage for QLS-LCC. However, the prospects of a QLS-level advantage do not necessarily translate to a speed-up in an end-to-end workflow. Finally, up to 28-qubit HHL-icMRLCCSD numerical calculations on potential energy curves of model systems containing up to four atoms recover the ground state energies with about $0.012\%$ errors relative to benchmark classical methods.
item.dc:creator: Peniel Bertrand Tsemo, Kenji Sugisaki, Ishita Bhattacharjee, V. S. Prasannaa

item.title: Atomic structure calculations for constraining new electron-electron forces
item.description: arXiv:2608.26532v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a general approach for calculating new electron-electron interactions with atomic structure theory, include dominant many-body effects, and extract bounds for parity-odd cases. The procedure is valid for any mediator mass and improves previous calculations by including many-body corrections to the new interaction through the time-dependent Hartree-Fock method. Bounds on coupling strengths are then extracted for scalar-pseudoscalar and vector-axial vector interactions by comparison with experimental atomic electric dipole moments and parity non-conserving (PNC) transitions respectively. In the latter case, our calculations rule out any coupling-mass ratio |g^e_V g^e_A|/m_X^2 greater than 10^-11 MeV^-2 above m_X ~ 10 MeV, covering a previously unconstrained mass region. We also report an updated calculation of the regular (Standard Model) electron-electron Z^0 exchange contribution to the 6s-7s PNC transition amplitude E_PNC in cesium.
item.dc:creator: Cameron J. West, Benjamin M. Roberts

item.title: Decay versus dephasing in Rydberg analog optimization: the exchange rate depends on the readout
item.description: arXiv:2608.29858v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Numerical studies of noisy Rydberg-atom optimization compress decoherence into a single rate, treating spontaneous decay ($\Gamma$) and dephasing ($\gamma$) as equivalent. We resolve the two as independent Lindblad axes for quantum annealing of unit-disk maximum independent set at fixed annealing time and ask how their relative effect depends on the readout. For the raw readout the size error collapses onto the effective dephasing rate $u=\kappa\Gamma+\gamma$, and at small noise a unit of decay rate degrades the result as much as $\kappa=7.4$ units of dephasing rate; a collapse fit across the whole grid returns 8.3. After greedy completion followed by a $(1,2)$-swap local search, classical post-processing of polynomial cost, the exchange rate falls to $\kappa=1.6$, and at the calibrated operating point of a commercial device dephasing produces three quarters of the noise-induced error instead of two fifths. First-order perturbation theory built from noiseless propagation gives the decay and dephasing susceptibilities of every readout, raw or post-processed, to a few parts in $10^6$ of the full Lindblad result. The raw asymmetry is set at the end of the schedule, where a decay event deletes an atom and a dephasing event leaves the readout unchanged. Post-processing refills most deletions and leaves misplaced atoms, which the two channels produce at comparable rates. Which channel limits a device therefore depends on the readout as well as on the hardware.
item.dc:creator: Seunghyeon Kim, Minjoo Kim, Junwoo Jung

item.title: Matrix Holography on an Optical Lattice
item.description: arXiv:2609.05613v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose an analog quantum-simulation protocol based on a lattice of atomic ensembles and time-averaged Floquet dynamics to construct the four-body potentials that typically appear in bosonic BFSS-like matrix quantum mechanics. In contrast to gate-based digital implementations requiring deep circuits, our approach generates the target model through a fixed set of control stages per Floquet cycle, keeping the number of consecutive unitaries constant with respect to the matrix size $N$. The principal scaling cost in our construction is given by the frequency range required to control the growing lattice. We show that this cost grows at most as $\mathcal{O}(N^3)$, giving a polynomial scaling route to large$-N$, attractive to experimental implementation. Additionally, we demonstrate that the coupling parameter can be tuned beyond $\mathcal{O}(1)$, enabling the simulation of strong-coupling physics necessary for holographic phases.
item.dc:creator: Robin L\"owenberg, Julian Sonner

item.title: Majorization for superpositions of nonorthogonal states and the existence of golden states
item.description: arXiv:2610.26483v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Golden states, from which every state can be prepared by free operations, are the units of a resource theory. In the resource theory of superposition relative to linearly independent, nonorthogonal reference states, they were known only for two reference states and for special overlap matrices, all of them maximally coherent in the L\"{o}wdin basis. We determine what decides their existence and when this L\"{o}wdin pattern holds. For every overlap matrix, the robustness and the geometric measure of superposition are maximized by the same states, which overlap equally with all reference states; the maximal values are set by the ground-state energy of a classical $XY$ model on the dual basis. These states, and only these, are golden under the maximal superposition-free operations, but they need not be maximally coherent in the L\"{o}wdin basis. For the Kraus-type free operations, we prove Gram majorization, a necessary and sufficient criterion for converting pure states into targets with nonzero coefficients, which reduces to majorization for orthonormal reference states. It shows that every golden state of these operations is maximally coherent in the L\"{o}wdin basis, yet golden states exist only for special overlap matrices: three reference states that are not orthonormal admit one if and only if their overlaps have a common modulus $s$ and their Bargmann phase $\Phi$ obeys $s\geq2\cos[(\pi+|\Phi|)/3]$, so that a geometric phase decides whether the theory has a unit. Finally, equal-overlap states yield a complete family of superposition witnesses in the L\"{o}wdin basis, which show that white noise is a resource unless the reference states are orthonormal.
item.dc:creator: G\"{o}khan Torun

item.title: Kelvin-Wave Multiplication by Sound Emission
item.description: arXiv:2610.39909v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Kelvin waves are bending excitations of a quantized vortex. We identify a subsonic decay channel in which one Kelvin quantum emits a phonon and splits into two lower-energy Kelvin quanta, reducing the Kelvin-wave energy while increasing the number of quanta. For sound wavelengths much longer than the Kelvin wavelengths, rotational symmetry fixes the leading shear contribution to the emission amplitude in terms of the released Kelvin energy. This contribution is odd in the phonon momentum along the vortex. Microscopic calculations support the relation. Coherently seeded Gross--Pitaevskii evolution in a reflecting cavity demonstrates phase-controlled Kelvin gain, with increased mean-square vortex displacement and reduced mean-square slope.
item.dc:creator: Weican Yang
